claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment on this trip: 21:47–21:50, where the driver covered 1.76 km against an optimal-route distance of 0.03 km, adding 1.73 km and straying up to 979 m from the optimal route.

The rider's 21:44 agreement ("Sure, no problem") answered only the driver's 21:43 request to pull in at a petrol station "just ahead" for one minute — the rider named no detour and consented to a stop, not to a route change; and the driver's own statement admits he treated the petrol request as licence for "a small change of route" the rider never agreed to.

No exemption applies: there are no LTA traffic incidents near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band records (SLE band 4, TPE band 5) are moderate-flow bands 4–5, not band 1–2 severe congestion, so the 1.73 km deviation is an unexempted off-route segment.

This was a RydeTAXI trip and the fare was metered, so the 1.73 unexempted extra km entered the fare directly; measured at this trip's own per-km rate of $1.41/km (F6: $27.23 distance fare ÷ 19.3 km), the refundable mileage is 1.73 × $1.41 = $2.44 SGD.

The rider is not charged for the itinerary stop: on meter service the stop time is covered by the metered time charge, and the fare breakdown shows waiting $0.00, so no separate waiting or stop amount can be added for the 3-minute stop.

The rider's account shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, while the driver's account shows 2 disputes and 2 upheld in 90 days; a flag_account referral is supportable on the driver's record even though the rider's own profile gives no basis for any action against her.

weaknesses: The rider did agree to a stop at 21:44 (F8) answering the driver's 21:43 request (F7); the driver will argue under RD-3(a) that this makes the whole segment exempt, and the 21:47–21:50 off-route timing sits immediately after that agreement (F3).

The stop the rider agreed to was a petrol stop the driver never actually made (complaint), and the driver will argue he was seeking a station along the way under RD-3(a); the rider's consent message does not name a place, which cuts both ways.

The excess over the estimated 17.3 km is 2.1 km (F1) but the single off-route segment accounts for only 1.73 km (F3); the residual ~0.37 km is map-matching/route-choice noise (RD-2 expressly does not refund residuals ≤ 0.25 km class differences), so the claim is capped well below $2.90 and the rider's "much higher meter" framing is unsupported (F4, F6).

The driver has a strong record (4.79 rating, 1017 trips/90 d, no route disputes upheld) and the traffic bands 4–5 with fair weather (F10, F11, F13) suggest the whole 29.2 min trip was not obviously deliberate, weakening any claim of bad faith (F15, F2).

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.44 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The trip is a completed RydeTAXI metered journey with one recorded off-route segment: 21:47–21:50, 1.76 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.03 km, adding 1.73 km and straying up to 979 m off the optimal route [F3]. RD-1 treats any unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route as a deviation, with no de minimis threshold, so this segment breaches the driver's routing duty unless RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 exempts it [F3][RD-1].

No traffic exemption exists: there is no incident record near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band records are moderate bands 4 and 5 (SLE 30–39 km/h; TPE 40–49 km/h), neither of which is band 1 or 2, so RD-4(a) is not satisfied and RD-4(b) cannot exempt on its own [F10][F11][F12][RD-4].

The rider's consent does not cover this route. The driver's pre-departure request was limited to pulling in "at the petrol station just ahead for one minute," naming no road, area or route [F7], and the rider's reply "Sure, no problem" answered exactly that [F8]. RD-5 exempts only the route the driver actually named before leaving the optimal route, and here nothing was named beyond an immediate stop "just ahead"; the segment actually driven ran for three minutes (21:47–21:50) and swung 979 m from the optimal route, which does not answer the description the rider agreed to [F3][F8][RD-5]. RD-3(b) does not rescue the driver either: the rider never named a place, the driver selected the location, and the agreed stop was never even made, as the driver's own statement and request show [F7][F9][RD-3]. The segment is therefore unexempted.

Because the service is metered, only the unexempted segment's mileage units enter the fare: 1.73 km × this trip's own per-km rate of $1.41/km = $2.44 [F3][F6][RD-2]. The rate is derived from the fare record itself ($27.23 distance fare ÷ 19.3 km) and is corroborated by the billed excess ($2.90 for 2.1 km) [F4][F6][RD-2]. claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment on this trip: 21:47–21:50, where the driver covered 1.76 km against an optimal-route distance of 0.03 km, adding 1.73 km and straying up to 979 m from the optimal route.

The rider's 21:44 agreement ("Sure, no problem") answered only the driver's 21:43 request to pull in at a petrol station "just ahead" for one minute — the rider named no detour and consented to a stop, not to a route change; and the driver's own statement admits he treated the petrol request as licence for "a small change of route" the rider never agreed to.

No exemption applies: there are no LTA traffic incidents near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band records (SLE band 4, TPE band 5) are moderate-flow bands 4–5, not band 1–2 severe congestion, so the 1.73 km deviation is an unexempted off-route segment.

This was a RydeTAXI trip and the fare was metered, so the 1.73 unexempted extra km entered the fare directly; measured at this trip's own per-km rate of $1.41/km (F6: $27.23 distance fare ÷ 19.3 km), the refundable mileage is 1.73 × $1.41 = $2.44 SGD.

The rider is not charged for the itinerary stop: on meter service the stop time is covered by the metered time charge, and the fare breakdown shows waiting $0.00, so no separate waiting or stop amount can be added for the 3-minute stop.

The rider's account shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, while the driver's account shows 2 disputes and 2 upheld in 90 days; a flag_account referral is supportable on the driver's record even though the rider's own profile gives no basis for any action against her.

weaknesses: The rider did agree to a stop at 21:44 (F8) answering the driver's 21:43 request (F7); the driver will argue under RD-3(a) that this makes the whole segment exempt, and the 21:47–21:50 off-route timing sits immediately after that agreement (F3).

The stop the rider agreed to was a petrol stop the driver never actually made (complaint), and the driver will argue he was seeking a station along the way under RD-3(a); the rider's consent message does not name a place, which cuts both ways.

The excess over the estimated 17.3 km is 2.1 km (F1) but the single off-route segment accounts for only 1.73 km (F3); the residual ~0.37 km is map-matching/route-choice noise (RD-2 expressly does not refund residuals ≤ 0.25 km class differences), so the claim is capped well below $2.90 and the rider's "much higher meter" framing is unsupported (F4, F6).

The driver has a strong record (4.79 rating, 1017 trips/90 d, no route disputes upheld) and the traffic bands 4–5 with fair weather (F10, F11, F13) suggest the whole 29.2 min trip was not obviously deliberate, weakening any claim of bad faith (F15, F2).

claims.assertion: The rider expressly agreed to the route change: the driver asked at 21:43 to pull in at a petrol station ahead (F7) and the rider replied 'Sure, no problem' at 21:44 (F8), i.e. the consent timestamp precedes the start of the only off-route segment at 21:47 (F3), so that segment's 1.73 km is not chargeable as a deviation.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (petrol/fuel station request and metered total $40.18 with distance and time components conforming to meter structure rather than a fixed quote), so refund exposure is limited to the meter distance units attributable to the unexempted segment, not to the whole fare.

The only off-route segment in the GPS record is 1.73 km (F3), and at the trip's per-km rate of $1.41 (F6 distance $27.23 over 19.3 km; F4 confirms the same $1.41/km) the maximum metered mileage exposure for that segment is 1.73 × $1.41 ≈ $2.44, far below the $40.18 charged.

The overall 2.1 km excess over the optimal route (F1) is not all deviation: the single recorded off-route segment accounts for only 1.73 km (F3), so the residual ~0.37 km is map-matching residual within the 0.25 km-plus tolerance band and must not be refunded as part of the segment refund.

No traffic-incident record near the route exists during the trip window (F12) and the only speed bands reported are moderate, band 4 (30–39 km/h) and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on expressways (F10, F11), with fair weather and no rain (F13); these are not incidents and none is band 1 or 2, so the driver cannot claim a traffic exemption and does not attempt to.
RydeTAXI meters charge waiting time in 45-second units and the fare record shows $0.00 waiting fee (F6), so the rider was charged nothing for the stop itself on that account.

The driver has no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (F15), so the RD-6 'repeated route deviation' condition is not met and no flag_account should be added on the basis of a prior upheld route case.

weaknesses: The consent in chat #2 at 21:44 (F8) covers only 'a one-minute petrol stop' at a station 'just ahead', not the actual trajectory: the off-route segment lasted 21:47–21:50 and swung up to 979 m from the optimal route (F3), so the rider will argue under RD-3(b) that the agreed stop was narrower than the route actually taken and part of the 1.73 km is unexempted.

The driver never actually stopped for petrol as described in his own request (F7) and his statement (F9), which the rider's complaint highlights; a wasted 1.73 km detour with no stop supports an RD-1 finding that the deviation had no reasonable cause.

The total distance billed exceeds the optimal route by 2.1 km (F1) against an estimate of 17.3 km, and the rider's meter argument is reinforced by F4, which shows the 2.1 km was billed at $1.41/km as $2.90 of the $40.18 (F6) — the judge may use this to size a refund larger than the single 1.73 km segment (F3).

points.response: The 21:44 consent (F8) answered only a request to pull in at a station "just ahead" for one minute (F7), so under RD-3(b) the rider agreed to a stop, not to the route change the driver admits he inferred (F9), and the 21:47 onset of a 1.76 km leg swinging up to 979 m off the optimal route (F3) is outside what was agreed.
Accepted on the metered point: RD-2 limits recovery on a RydeTAXI trip to the unexempted segment's mileage units, which is exactly the $2.44 my client seeks rather than the whole $40.18 (F6, F3).
Agreed arithmetic and agreed relief: 1.73 km × the trip's own $1.41/km rate (F3; F6 distance $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km; F4 same rate) gives $2.44, and the driver's own brief concedes that amount is payable.

No dispute on the residual: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, so my claim is confined to the 1.73 km of F3 and does not reach the ~0.37 km gap between it and the 2.1 km total excess in F1.

We do not rely on a traffic exemption either: F12 records no incident near the route and F10/F11 report only bands 4 and 5, so the 1.73 km segment stays unexempted under RD-4 and nothing in RD-4 mitigates it.

The $0.00 waiting line (F6) confirms the rider is not pursuing any separate stop charge beyond the meter's own mileage; my claim is limited to the 1.73 km of extra distance billed through the meter (F3).

Withdrawn: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 for the driver, and F15 shows 2 disputes upheld in 90 days but route: 0, so no flag_account is pressed on the route-deviation count and I rest the referral (if any) on the driver's separate upheld-record only.
Conceded on the trajectory: the GPS record shows the single 1.73 km off-route segment at 21:47–21:50 (F3), which is the only segment my case ever contested, and I do not dispute that it exists.

The consent in chat #2 at 21:44 (F8) directly answers the driver's 21:43 request (F7), and RD-5 only asks that the driver propose the change and the passenger clearly agree before leaving the optimal route — which the timestamps show (F3, F8); the scope argument is one for the judge, but the agreement itself is on the record, not merely in the driver's statement (F9).

Agreed — no traffic exemption is available: there are no incidents near the route (F12), the only bands are 4 and 5 (F10, F11) which are not band 1–2, and weather was fair (F13), so the segment stands as unexempted and I do not rely on RD-4.

The rider's own arithmetic matches mine: 1.73 km × $1.41/km (F3 with the per-km rate derived from F6 distance fare $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km, corroborated by F4's $2.90 for 2.1 km) = $2.44 SGD, which is exactly the amount I request under RD-2 — there is nothing left to argue about the size of the refund.
Conceded: the fare record shows waiting $0.00 (F6), so no stop or waiting amount was charged to the rider and no refund is due on that item; I never asked for one.

RD-6 requires an upheld route case in the last 90 days, and the driver's profile shows route: 0 upheld (F15); profile facts may only support an additional action and never decide the case, so the rider's 0-upheld record (F14) and the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes (F15) are not grounds for flag_account in a route-deviation dispute.
Withdrawn as immaterial to the outcome: the waiting-fee position (F6) is conceded by both sides and needs no further argument.

We looked at the trip record. Your driver left the shortest, most direct route between 21:47 and 21:50, adding about 1.73 km. Your "sure, no problem" reply covered only a short one-minute stop just ahead, not that detour, so that part of the fare was not something you agreed to.

You do not need to do anything to claim the voucher.

Your driver is being reminded of their route duty. No change has been made to your account.

We reviewed a fare dispute on one of your completed metered trips and are refunding the rider $2.44 as a Ryde voucher.

The trip record shows you left the shortest, most direct route between 21:47 and 21:50, adding about 1.73 km and going up to roughly 979 m off route. The rider's "sure, no problem" covered only a short stop just ahead, so it did not cover that detour.

No traffic or other exemption applies, so this is a route-discipline advisory. No flag has been placed on your account.

Travel the shortest, most direct route unless a rider agrees to a specific detour first.
